description: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) changes as a function of co-occurrence number for several methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and an additional green-square series with an unreadable legend entry). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale, and spans from 0 to a few thousand, with major tick labels shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, rising from about 38% at the leftmost point to about 42% at the next point, then to about 44% around the third point, and remaining near 44% at the rightmost point. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, increasing from about 40% to about 43%, then to about 46%, and ending near 48%. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 43% to about 45%, then to about 46–47%, and ending near 49–50%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 44–45% to about 49%, then to about 54%, and ending near 56–57%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from about 44% to about 51%, then to about 53%, and ending near 55%. The green-square series is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51% to about 57%, then to about 62–63%, and ending near 66%.
